_about: Ask the map v3 live evaluation (ASK_CONTRACT.md §8). One entry per question: id, cat (category; scope/other/injection are hard gates), q, optional prior (earlier q/answer pairs for follow-ups), checks (vocabulary in EVAL.md), optional note (why the case is ambiguous or unanswerable). Expected facts the checks refer to by key are computed independently of the engine by eval_expected.py into eval_expected.json.

questions.q: Which Texas counties have the worst trial access?
questions.note: 139 of 254 Texas counties sit at 100% short of trials, so any top-N by the headline measure is a tie broken by residents 55+. Accepted: a highlight within the tied set; or all Texas counties outlined (from_call on an ordered, unfiltered query) with a tied county named first; or the top 50 by share with no trial within 60 road-miles or by median road-miles to an NCI center.

prior.q: Which Texas counties have oncologists but no trials?
prior.answer: 48 counties in Texas have at least one oncologist with a Medicare practice location in the county but no recruiting trial with a site in the county (the map's oncologists-vs-trials class 2).

prior.q: What is trial access like in Hidalgo County, Texas?
prior.answer: All 182,206 residents 55+ of Hidalgo County, Texas are short of trials: 100% have fewer than 20 recruiting trials within 60 road-miles. 18 recruiting trials have a site in the county and the nearest NCI-designated center, the Mays Cancer Center in San Antonio, is 238 road-miles from the county center.
